name: White nationalism
summary: White nationalism holds that white people form a race and nation whose survival, culture and political and demographic dominance should be secured, usually through white-majority or all-white states and sharply restricted non-white immigration. Adherents treat racial differences as largely innate, reject racial equality as a goal and often claim that elites are engineering white decline. Leading figures present it as separation rather than supremacy, which critics dispute, and its economic and religious views vary widely.
scope: The mainstream of the self-described white nationalist movement as represented by Jared Taylor and American Renaissance, with Greg Johnson, Richard Spencer and the Fourteen Words milieu as reference points. It does not cover white supremacy as a wider doctrine (a separate profile), nor civic or non-racial nationalisms that critics label white nationalist. Taylor's White Identity (2011) is the primary text; economic and religious positions are largely unsettled and answered low.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No shared position; the movement's economic strands split.

unions-good.rationale: Economics is secondary to race and strands differ on labor.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are not a defining issue; some strands are libertarian, others reject it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Some strands attack corporations as multicultural, others favor free enterprise.

cut-welfare.rationale: Taylor treats welfare as having failed to fix black and Hispanic poverty, and American Renaissance ties welfare to birth rates.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents favor border and security control but also fear state surveillance of themselves.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Taylor frames his case as free speech and sued over suspension; adherents see hate-speech law as aimed at them.

strong-leader.rationale: Some strands, notably the alt-right, favor strong leadership; others stress representative government.

state-harmful.rationale: The program requires a state to secure a racial homeland and borders, so the state is not seen as harmful.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents stress white birth rates and families, and the Fourteen Words speak of a future for white children.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Most adherents oppose it though some, such as Greg Johnson, urge tolerance of gay members.

abortion-legal.rationale: Many leading figures oppose abortion because of falling white birth rates, but some, such as Spencer, accept it on eugenic grounds, so the movement is split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents hold varied faiths, including atheism and paganism, so there is no shared line.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Taylor treats racial preferences for blacks and Hispanics as unfair to whites and too entrenched for legislatures to abolish, though he never sets out a call to end them; opposing race-conscious remedies follows from the movement's focus on white interests.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Culture is held to be a product of race and white culture should be foremost in white-majority countries.

gradual-change.rationale: Taylor presents himself as moderate while others seek radical change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Taylor says immigration should be cut close to zero and restricted to Europeans in most American strands.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents defend national and racial sovereignty and distrust global bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Economics is not defining and strands differ.

nation-first.rationale: Interests of the white nation or race come first, though pan-white solidarity cuts across it.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders are the opposite of the demand to keep white majorities.

revolution-justified.rationale: Prominent figures stress peaceful, metapolitical change, though violent strands exist.

experts-over-public.rationale: Adherents distrust academic experts yet cite race science.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism is common among strands, but not universal.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: This is not a common theme in the movement's writings.

one-party-rule.rationale: Taylor names representative government as a European principle to preserve.

democracy-best.rationale: Taylor values representative government, but democracy is not defended when it produces demographic change.

political-violence-never.rationale: Leading figures disavow violence, but the milieu includes terrorism and the Fourteen Words.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Only Christian Identity strands favor it; most do not.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The defining aim is a state, or states, made up of one race or ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Ethnic conflict, not class, is held to drive history; Taylor says history is the history of warfare.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Racial gaps are attributed to innate differences, so equal outcomes are rejected.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents reject racial redress and treat Western civilization as a benefit.

civilizational-union.rationale: White nationalism is a pan-nationalism that unites whites across states.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Group interest is affirmed, individual self-interest is not a doctrinal point.

limit-population.rationale: Pronatalist for whites, though some want others' growth limited.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Western civilization is treated as an achievement to preserve.

restore-past-order.rationale: Aims to preserve or restore the white-majority society of the past, though framed as survival not nostalgia.

direct-action.rationale: Figures like Greg Johnson stress cultural, metapolitical work and electoral influence.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marxist idea alien to the movement.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist claim alien to the movement.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Ethnic conflict, not capitalism, is cited as the cause of war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a defining claim; some libertarian-leaning strands hold it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Group racial interests and identity are held legitimate.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents say media and academia enforce anti-white orthodoxy; Taylor says whites cannot discuss race honestly.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial differences in ability and behavior are a core claim of Taylor and American Renaissance.

total-state.rationale: Most adherents do not seek a total state, though fascist strands do.

national-rebirth.rationale: Adherents warn of white decline and oblivion and call for a racial reawakening.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ethnonationalists favor homogeneous homelands over multiethnic empire.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Adherents claim objective race science is suppressed.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Adherents are split: many oppose Zionism, while Taylor and some others admire Israel as an ethnostate.

national-self-determination.rationale: Each ethnic group should have a sovereign homeland, and Taylor says people should not share one society.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Adherents hold religious and secular views.

class-collaboration.rationale: Racial solidarity is placed above class.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preservation of Western civilization and heritage is central.

workers-nation.rationale: Racial and national identity over class internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Adherents favor traditional gender roles and early childbearing by white women.

ban-interest.rationale: Some antisemitic strands oppose usury, but most do not.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Taylor favors voluntary segregation and separate homelands rather than law classifying citizens, though some strands go further.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Culture is seen as racial, so assimilation of non-whites is thought not to work; exclusion is preferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: The white genocide or replacement claim, that elites push immigration to displace whites, is widely held, with Taylor and Lane among its proponents.

national-mission.rationale: Ethnonationalists favor separation over spreading institutions abroad.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Taylor calls government a government of traitors and elites are accused of betraying whites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Taylor proposed implantable contraceptives for welfare mothers, and eugenics is common in the milieu.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Strands differ on the scope of state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Many adherents believe miscegenation threatens the white race, though Taylor opposes laws against it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Adherents reject racial equality as a goal and say whites are denied group interests, while denying supremacy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Taylor wants America to remain a European-majority nation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Taylor frames majority preference as a legitimate basis for law.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism is common but not defining.

population-transfer.rationale: Some adherents back remigration and Spencer called for "peaceful ethnic cleansing", while others reject it, so the movement is split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Leading figures disavow violence but the movement contemplates coercive separation and includes violent strands.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist and group-conflict themes recur; Taylor says history is warfare.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents see such bans as targeting them.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Adherents blame group traits and welfare-driven birth rates rather than population as such.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Taylor argues diversity is a source of conflict, not strength, and that multiracial societies are doomed to failure.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Economic positions are largely unsettled in the movement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Organizations differ and the main texts do not address party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The movement is nation- and race-first and generally rejects the EU as a vehicle of mass immigration, though some favour pan-European white unity.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religious views vary widely across the movement.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adherents are split: some want cultural standards, but many present themselves as victims of censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The movement has no settled view on executive term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: The movement has no settled view on recall of officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents split between isolationists and those who want white-world solidarity; the movement states no alliance doctrine.

people-in-arms.rationale: Gun rights are popular in the American milieu, but no doctrine of replacing the army is stated; adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Taylor holds that races differ innately in ability and that civilizations differ in achievement, rejecting equality of groups.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Adherents split between religious and secular or pagan strands and the movement has no school-curriculum line.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The movement has no stated view on how constitutions should be remade; strands differ.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Strands differ; some favour authoritarian means for racial ends, others stress free speech.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Economic views vary widely, as the audit scope notes.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The USSR's economic character is not a movement issue; strands differ.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Economics is largely unsettled in the movement and adherents are split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Taylor holds that racial differences are largely innate and not erased by environment.

land-redistribution.rationale: Never a core question; economic positions are largely unsettled and expropriation is generally disfavoured.

refugee-return.rationale: Never a settled question; adherents' views on refugees' right of return are unrecorded.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Some leaders such as Spencer argue for white unity across borders, but this is not the mainstream position.

ban-cartels.rationale: Economic positions are largely unsettled, so no inference is made.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic positions are largely unsettled, so no inference is made.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Taylor's White Identity attacks racial preferences in hiring and admissions as discrimination against whites and welcomes ballot initiatives that abolished them. White nationalists are not race-blind, but on preferences for non-whites they agree strongly.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not a stated doctrine; strands differ on class and economics.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Taylor argues that anti-discrimination law infringes freedom of association and that whites should be free to prefer their own.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No settled position; some adherents distrust constitutional limits that protect minorities while valuing white-majority rule.

office-by-exam.rationale: Adherents are split; hereditarian views of ability sit beside distrust of establishment institutions.

recallable-delegates.rationale: No settled position; populist accountability and elite distrust pull in different directions.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Economic positions are largely unsettled among adherents.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Adherents reject racial equality as a goal and oppose anti-discrimination enforcement based on outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Some leading figures criticise consumer materialism and liberal modernity; not central.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents split between law-and-order nationalists and those who see the present legal order as illegitimate; no settled position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The replacement narrative blames a Jewish-led elite for white decline, but Taylor and others decline the Jewish question, so strands are split.

local-production.rationale: Some strands favor economic nationalism and localism, others market positions; not a defining issue, so split.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by race, not faith; religion is left to individuals and strands range from Christian to pagan to secular.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Sources address welfare only as limited to whites; public service delivery models are unsettled among adherents.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Adherents are split: figures such as Jared Taylor distance themselves from outright denial while parts of the wider milieu embrace it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Adherents differ; the sources describe traditional-family conservatism in much of the movement but no settled demand to criminalise same-sex relations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religious views in the movement vary widely, and the sources give no demand for state punishment of blasphemy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Taylor and the movement reject racial equality as a goal and deny that racism or privilege structures explain disparities.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Religious views in the movement vary from Christian Identity to paganism and atheism, so there is no shared position.

social-market-economy.rationale: The sources describe the movement's economic views as widely varied, with welfare supported for citizens in some strands and cut in others.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement stresses national survival, military strength and homeland defence, so abolishing armed forces runs against its core.

rich-first.rationale: The sources report no settled stance on this development principle, and economic views vary in the movement.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement's franchise criterion is race, not property; property qualifications are not part of its programme.

reification.rationale: A Marxist analysis of capitalism that the movement rejects; it attributes social ills to race and elites, not to reification.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Its marriage restrictions are racial, not religious; religious intermarriage rules are not part of its mainstream.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Adherents are split: antisemitic strands favour such boycotts, while the mainstream presenting itself as separation not supremacy avoids them.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement stresses law and order and ethnic security; abolition of policing is foreign to it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Economic views are largely unsettled across white nationalist strands, ranging from market to welfare positions.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Religious views vary widely, from Christian Identity to paganism to secularism, so adherents are split.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement has no common line on unions and strands differ on economics.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Economic questions are largely unsettled in the movement and strands differ.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Some strands favour secession and local homelands, but the movement has no common line.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Religious views vary widely across the movement, from Christian to pagan to secular.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Taylor's White Identity argues that whites should recognise and organise around their group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: White Identity and American Renaissance present white racial consciousness and pride as legitimate and necessary.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Economic views vary widely and unions are not a defining issue; adherents split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not a defining issue and economic views differ across the movement.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Adherents want a white homeland and see the state as hostile to whites, but mainstream figures such as Taylor do not call for revolution; split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Economic organisation is largely unsettled in the movement, so adherents are split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The movement has no settled stance on pricing nature.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm support is not a defining issue and strands differ; some agrarian and blood-and-soil strands favor it, others free markets.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Economic views vary widely across the movement, so adherents are split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Religious views vary widely, with Christian, pagan and secular strands.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Many adherents favour ethnostates or rule by a racial community over open electoral competition; not uniform.

women-suffrage.rationale: Adherents are split, with some traditionalist strands opposing equal political roles.

race-social-construct.rationale: Taylor's White Identity argues races are real biological groupings, rejecting the social-construct view.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Religious views vary widely, from Christian Identity to paganism to secularism, so no common line on scripture is stated.

simple-living.rationale: No stated position; the sources are silent on austerity or self-sufficiency and adherents are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Adherents hold that whites need a homeland of their own and a duty to preserve it, though Taylor argues in terms of identity more than spirituality.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Adherents care for people of European descent beyond their borders, for example white South Africans, as part of white interests.

self-ownership.rationale: Collectivist race thinking and libertarian strands coexist and the movement has no settled view.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Adherents are split; the movement is hostile to elites but not systematically anti-party.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Economic views are unsettled and the issue is peripheral to the movement.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Religion is not central and adherents range from Christian identity to pagan and secular; split.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The movement is not defined by a view on divorce, and traditionalist and secular strands differ.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Taylor and American Renaissance attribute racial gaps largely to innate differences, not to racism as the main obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Adherents are split, wanting law and order but rejecting anti-discrimination law as illegitimate.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The movement has no settled view on automation and adherents split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Racial identity is its central concern, ahead of class or material interests.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Taylor treats welfare as having failed to fix black and Hispanic poverty, and American Renaissance ties welfare to birth rates. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Ethnic and racial diversity makes a society less cohesive and more prone to conflict.
missingStatements.rationale: Taylor argues diversity is a source of conflict, not strength, and cites ethnic conflict as the main cause of instability in multiethnic states.

missingStatements.text: Employers, schools and landlords should be free to discriminate on the basis of race.
missingStatements.rationale: Taylor frames segregation as free association and opposes anti-discrimination laws, though he does not call for mandated separation.
missingStatements.declined: Peripheral to the doctrine, which stresses separation and immigration; hate-speech, racial-segregation-law and correct-racial-injustice already capture the contested anti-discrimination question loosely.

notes: Strands differ sharply: Taylor and Johnson present white nationalism as non-supremacist separation, while Lane and neo-Nazi strands are openly supremacist and violent. Economics, religion and the Jewish question are split, so those answers are low confidence or neutral. Sources are partly critical (SPLC), and Taylor's text was read in part.
